Provides the ability to search for news relevant to economy of a region: 
 * FIPS - Querying by FIPS code returns only news articles that have been written about events that have occurred within the given county or CBSA. FIPS codes for counties can be found [here](https://www.census.gov/prod/techdoc/cbp/95-96cd/fips-st.pdf). FIPS codes for CBSAs can be found [here](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cps/methodology/2015%20Geography%20Cover.pdf). Maps of CBSAs can be found [here](https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-maps/2020/geo/cbsa.html). 
 * Free Form Text Search - A search for words or phrases can be performed against the articles matching any of the previous options listed. 
 * Significance - Articles are classified by their significance. A highly significant article is one that is alert worthy whereas less significant articles are more relevant when performing research. This option will filter the results returned by the previous options listed. 
 

 The following is an example of using the API. 

 To query for the economic news about the Los Angeles region using the FIPS code 037 between 7/1/2018 and 7/31/2018 : 

 ```js
 GET https://api.bitvore.com/v2/corp/econnews?fips=037&startDate=2018-07-01T00:00:00.000+07:00&endDate=2018-07-31T23:59:59.999+07:00
 ```

Provides a simple GET oriented corporate news search capability. The search criteria used when querying news includes the following options specified as query parameters which can used together to refine the search results: 
 * Bitvore ID - A Bitvore ID, known as a BvID, uniquely identifies a company/organization. Querying by BvID returns only news articles where the identified company is an actor in the story.
 * Signal - An article can be classified by one or more signals indicating that the article describes an event, or events, identified in the Bitvore Signal taxonomy. The taxonomy is hierarchical and signal values are '.' encoded to represent that hierarchy, i.e., Labor.Hiring. Querying by signal returns only articles classified by the given signal. All child signals in the signal hierarchy will also be returned. For example querying for Labor will return Labor.Hiring and Labor.Strike articles. The signals currently supported can be found [here](http://developer.bitvore.com/v2/docs/api-reference/signals).
 * Free Form Text Search - A search for words or phrases can be performed against the articles matching any of the previous options listed. 
 * Article Type - Type of articles to return, News or PressRelease. By default all types are returned.
 * Significance - Articles are classified by their significance. A highly significant article is one that is alert worthy whereas less significant articles are more relevant when performing research. This option will filter the results returned by the previous options listed. 
 * Similarity - Indicates which (if any) similar articles should be returned, options are 
 "Usage" and "None", default is "None". "Usage" indicates similar articles can be returned if they 
 have different usage restrictions. In other word with this option two similar articles can be returned 
 if one is FullUse and the other is FairUse. 
 * Org Field - By default each company referenced in an article is identified by its ID and its name. Additional fields will be returned for each company if specified here. The available options are name, domainName, ticker, city, state, and country. If available the additional fields will be returned in the Org objects (ReferencedOrgs, MatchedOrgs, and MatchedArticleOrgs) in the article. Note: Returning additional fields may cause a small increase in latency. 
 

 The following are some examples of using the API. 

 To query for M&A news between 7/1/2018 and 7/31/2018 : 

 ```js
 GET https://api.bitvore.com/v2/corp/news?signal=MergerAcquisition&startDate=2018-07-01T00:00:00.000+07:00&endDate=2018-07-31T23:59:59.999+07:00
 ```
 

 The metadata tags of articles returned specific to corporate news in addition to the common tags above are: 
 * Signals - 0 or more signals detected in the article encoded with '.' notation such as Labor.Hiring. 
 * Referenced Orgs - 0 or more BvID/Name combinations identifying companies discussed in the article. 
 

 A sample successful response is: 

 ```js
 {
 	"success": true,
 	"returned": 1,
 	"total": 1,
 	"response": [
 		{
 			"key": "070000015cf083aba01f0826ecfe718e965b577c572166b14a77651c",
 			"articleType": "News",
 			"title": "ACME aquires Wile E. Coyote",
 			"sourceName": "acme.com",
 			"sourceUrl": "http://ct.moreover.com/?a=41646891667&p=5jw&v=1&x=yg6DsqTFf8IC8ym026-o0A",
 			"previewImageUrl": "http://acme.com/resources/coyote.jpg",
 			"excerpt": "The ACME corporation has completed the merger with Wile E. Coyote today ...",
 			"signals": ["MergeAcquisition.AcquisitionComplete"],
 			"referencedOrgs": [ 
 				{ "bvId" : "a00001aaa", "name" : "ACME Corp" }, 
 				{ "bvId" : "a00001aab", "name" : "Wile E. Coyote Inc" } 
 			],
 			"matchedArticleOrgs": [ 
 				{ "bvId" : "a00001aaa", "name" : "ACME Corp" } 
 			],
 			"matchedOrgs": [ 
 				{ "bvId" : "a00001aac", "name" : "A Company Manufacturing Everything" } 
 			],
 			"significance": "HIGH",
 			"sentiment" : 0.22555919, 
 			"esgSentiment" : 0.78078979, 
 			"articleLocations": ["United States"],
 			"sourceLocation": "Germany",
 			"publishedAt": "2017-06-29T21:41:19.109Z",
 			"availableAt": "2017-06-29T21:41:21.109Z",
 		}
 	]
 }
 ```
 

 Each article returned may have one or more groups of referenced articles. The referencedOrgs property holds the list of companies that were directly mentioned in the article and were considered the primary actors. In this example the article was about ACME merging with Wile E. Coyote which were considered the primary actors. 

 If there is more than one primary actor in an article it is often the case that only a subset of those actors were in the original scope of the input query (bvIds or portfolio). The matchedArticleOrgs will hold that subset of primary actors which were part of the input query. The system will look for articles about subsidiaries of the companies in the original scope of the input query as well. When a subsidiary is the primary actor of a returned article it will be in the referencedOrgs and matchedArticlesOrg field, but the parent company that was specified in the query will be returned in the matchedOrgs property. 

 In this example the original query was for articles about A Company Manufacturing Everything. The system found this article about its child company ACME. Therefore matchedArticleOrgs lists ACME and matchedOrgs lists A Company Manufacturing Everything which was in the original query. 

 A sample unsuccessful response is: 

 ```js
 {
 	"success": false,
 	"reason": "Bad bvId found",
 	"reasonSupport": "123456789 987654321",
 	"count": 0
 }
 ```

Provides an advanced corporate news search capability. The search criteria used when querying news includes a more advanced approach to identifying the company, or organization, scope of the news to return as well as the other content oriented options listed above. The following are the options supported for identifying the organization scope: 
 * Bitvore ID - A Bitvore ID, known as a BvID, uniquely identifies a company/organization. Querying by BvID returns only news articles where the identified company is an actor in the story.
 * Portfolio - A portfolio is made up of one or more companies (BvIDs). Querying by portfolio returns only articles where at least one of the companies in the portfolio are an actor in the article. This option cannot be used with the BvID or Foreign ID options. 
 * Foreign ID - If the Identification API is used to map BvIDs to ID's foreign to the Bitvore system the ID's mapped to BvIDs are considered foreign ID's which can be used using this parameter instead of a BvID. This option cannot be used with the BvID or Portfolio options. 
 * Employees - Returns all articles referencing companies with an estimated number of employees that falls within a specified range using the format of lower-upper, i.e. 50-250. The upper bound may be omitted (50-) to indicate an unbounded range. The ranges must be defined using the predefined measurements: 1, 10, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000. This option cannot be used with the BvID, Foreign ID, or Portfolio options. Note: On 1/11/2020 the range boundary of 200 was replaced by 100 and 250 and will be no longer supported on 7/1/2020. 
 * Revenue - Returns all articles referencing companies with an estimated revenue that falls within a specified range using the format of lower-upper, i.e. 500-1000. The upper bound may be omitted (500-) to indicate an unbounded range. The ranges must be defined using the predefined measurements:  0, 1, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 10000. This option cannot be used with the BvID, Foreign ID, or Portfolio options. Note: On 1/11/2020 the range boundary of 200 was replaced with 500 and will be no longer supported on 7/1/2020. 
 * NAICS Industry - Returns all articles referencing companies operating within the industry identified by the specified [NAICS](https://www.naics.com/search/) code. 
 * SIC Industry - Returns all articles referencing companies operating within the industry identified by the specified [SIC](https://www.osha.gov/pls/imis/sicsearch.html) code. 
 * HQ Location - Returns all articles referencing companies whose headquarters is located in the specified location. The location is in the format of city/state/country, i.e., Los Angeles/California/United States. 
 * HQ FIPS Area - Returns all articles referencing companies whose headquarters is located in the county or CBSA identified by the given FIPS code. FIPS codes for counties can be found [here](https://www.census.gov/prod/techdoc/cbp/95-96cd/fips-st.pdf). FIPS codes for CBSAs can be found [here](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cps/methodology/2015%20Geography%20Cover.pdf). Maps of CBSAs can be found [here](https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-maps/2020/geo/cbsa.html). 
 

 The following content oriented query options are also supported: 
 * Signal - An article can be classified by one or more signals indicating that the article describes an event, or events, identified in the Bitvore Signal taxonomy. The taxonomy is hierarchical and signal values are '.' encoded to represent that hierarchy, i.e., Labor.Hiring. Querying by signal returns only articles classified by the given signal. All child signals in the signal hierarchy will also be returned. For example querying for Labor will return Labor.Hiring and Labor.Strike articles. The signals currently supported can be found [here](https://api.bitvore.com/v2/docs/api-reference/signals).
 * Free Form Text Search - A search for words or phrases can be performed against the articles matching any of the previous options listed. 
 * Article Type - Type of articles to return, News or PressRelease. By default all types are returned.
 * Significance - Articles are classified by their significance. A highly significant article is one that is alert worthy whereas less significant articles are more relevant when performing research. This option will filter the results returned by the previous options listed. 
 * Usage - A news article may have licensing restrictions placed on it. To filter search 
 results to only fair use content specify "FairUse" for the Usage option. To filter results to only 
 commercially licensed content that grants full use of the content specify "FullUse" for the Usage option. 
 Specifying "All", which is the default option, does not filter the results at all. 
 * Org Field - By default each company referenced in an article is identified by its ID and its name. Additional fields will be returned for each company if specified here. The available options are name, domainName, ticker, city, state, and country. If available the additional fields will be returned in the Org objects (ReferencedOrgs, MatchedOrgs, and MatchedArticleOrgs) in the article. Note: Returning additional fields may cause a small increase in latency.
 

 The following are some examples of using the API. 

 To query for the news about IBM, BvID b00001ab7, published within the last 3 days in the PST timezone (using HTTP header for api key): 

 ```js
 POST https://api.bitvore.com/v2/corp/news 
 Accept: application/json
 X-BV-APIKEY: xyz123... 

 { 
 	"orgScope": { 
 		"ids": ["b00001ab7"], 
 		"orgIdScheme": "BVID" 
 	}, 
 	"startDate": "2018-07-01T09:00:00.000+07:00", 
 	"endDate": "2018-07-03T23:59:59.999+07:00" 
 } 
 ```
 

 To query for the news about all executive changes between 9:00AM PST 7/1/2018 and 5:00PM PST on 7/31/2018: 

 ```js
 POST https://api.bitvore.com/v2/corp/news 
 Accept: application/json
 X-BV-APIKEY: xyz123... 

 { 
 	"signal": ["ExecutiveChanges"], 
 	"startDate": "2018-07-01T09:00:00.000+07:00", 
 	"endDate": "2018-07-31T17:00:00.000+07:00" 
 } 
 ```
 

 To query for the news about a companies with annual revenue between 50M and 100M in the last 30 days: 

 ```js
 POST https://api.bitvore.com/v2/corp/news 
 Accept: application/json
 X-BV-APIKEY: xyz123... 

 { 
 	"orgScope": { 
 		"revRange": "50-100" 
 	}, 
 	"startDate": "2018-07-01T09:00:00.000Z", 
 	"endDate": "2018-07-31T17:00:00.000Z" 
 } 
 ```

 * Organization Id - An ID that uniquely identifies a company/organization. Querying by ID returns only news articles where the identified organization is an actor in the story. The organization's primary ID is always a BvID, however, if using an alternate ID, it will also be returned along with the organization. 
 * Org Id Scheme - The type of Id being used. Can be BvID, CUSIP, FIGI, ISIN or SEDOL. Certain IDs require a valid license. 
 * Signal - An article can be classified by one or more signals indicating that the article describes an event, or events, identified in the Bitvore Signal taxonomy. The taxonomy is hierarchical and signal values are '.' encoded to represent that hierarchy, i.e., Labor.Hiring. Querying by signal returns only articles classified by the given signal. All child signals in the signal hierarchy will also be returned. For example querying for Labor will return Labor.Hiring and Labor.Strike articles. The signals currently supported can be found [here](http://developer.bitvore.com/v2/docs/api-reference/signals).
 * Free Form Text Search - A search for words or phrases can be performed against the articles matching any of the previous options listed. 
 * Article Type - Type of articles to return, News or PressRelease. By default all types are returned.
 * Significance - Articles are classified by their significance. A highly significant article is one that is alert worthy whereas less significant articles are more relevant when performing research. This option will filter the results returned by the previous options listed. 
 * Similarity - Indicates which (if any) similar articles should be returned, options are 
 "Usage" and "None", default is "None". "Usage" indicates similar articles can be returned if they 
 have different usage restrictions. In other word with this option two similar articles can be returned 
 if one is FullUse and the other is FairUse. 
 * Org Field - By default each company referenced in an article is identified by its ID and its name. Additional fields will be returned for each company if specified here. The available options are name, domainName, ticker, city, state, and country. If available the additional fields will be returned in the Org objects (ReferencedOrgs, MatchedOrgs, and MatchedArticleOrgs) in the article.
